sections.html:
Jackson County runs along the California line in southern Oregon, with Medford as its seat. It covers 2,802 square miles and had 223,259 people in 2020, most of them in the Rogue Valley along the Bear Creek corridor that links Ashland, Talent, Phoenix, Medford and Central Point. Medford itself had 85,824.

The county has 11 incorporated cities and 34 unincorporated communities. A house can sit inside a city, in a small community with its own fire district, or on rural land outside any city, and the taxing districts on the bill change from one address to the next.

Health care, orchards, wine, a university and a theater festival bring in varied buyers, from hospital staff to retirees to orchard and vineyard owners. Condition and location still drive price more than any single employer.

sections.h2: Heat, fire and what they mean for a house
sections.html:
Medford has a dry Mediterranean climate, about 18.43 inches of precipitation a year, and the wear on a roof and cooling system shows it. The city averages about 61 afternoons above 90 degrees Fahrenheit and 11 above 100 each year. Winter is mild but not frost free, with freezing mornings on roughly 64 days a year.

Fire is the larger risk. The Almeda Drive Fire started on September 8, 2020, near Ashland and reached Phoenix and Talent within hours. It burned about 3,200 acres and destroyed more than 3,000 structures. Houses that were damaged, rebuilt or left vacant afterward often come with unusual tax and insurance questions.

If your Jackson County property was damaged, ask the Assessor's Office how the loss is reflected in its value before you set a price.

Property tax here splits between two county offices. The Assessor's Office values property, keeps the maps and ownership records, handles exemptions and oversees farm and forest special assessments. The Taxation office in the Finance Department collects the money.

OfficeContact
Assessor541-774-6059; Assessor@jacksoncountyor.gov
Taxation541-774-6541; taxation@jacksoncountyor.gov
Both offices10 S Oakdale Ave, Medford, OR 97501 (Taxation counter in Room 111A, Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM)

The Assessor values residential, commercial and business personal property, plus industrial land and improvements under $1,000,000, and verifies sales to track the market. The county also posts a Summary of Assessment and Levies report each fall.

Everything starts on November 15, and settling the whole bill by that day earns a 3% discount. Statements are sent by October 25. If the 15th is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, you get until the next business day. Ask the office to confirm the date in those years.

  • Whole bill by November 15: you save 3%.
  • Pay two-thirds by that date: you save 2%, and the remainder is due May 15.
  • One-third by that date: no discount, then more is due February 15 and May 15.
  • Interest of 1.333% a month (16% a year) starts on December 16, February 16 and May 16 for the three installments.

Mailed checks need a postmark dated on or before the due date, but mail consolidation means a local postmark may never be applied, which is a risk close to the deadline. Drop boxes are open around the clock, and payments there are credited the same day. Payments go first to fees, then to the oldest tax year owed.

Paying online by credit card adds a processor fee of 2.40% with a $2.00 minimum. Debit is 1% with the same minimum, and an e-check is $2.50. The county receives no part of those fees. Phone payments go through 541-774-6541. Prepayment is generally refused, except for omitted property or estimated tax on a new partition, plat or subdivision.

Your petition is filed with the Property Value Appeals Board clerk. You can file once your tax statement arrives, up to December 31 (the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday).

If you lose before the board, the Oregon Tax Court Magistrate Division is next, and a value appeal has a 30 day clock. Appeals about exemptions, special assessment disqualification or omitted property have a 90 day window. The Magistrate Division is at 1163 State St, Salem.

An appeal changes value only. It does not erase a bill that is already due, so a seller facing a closing date should pay what the county asks and treat any refund as a later matter.

Delinquent notices go out by mail in mid-June, with 1.333% monthly interest on every missed installment. ORS 312.010 allows foreclosure on real property when three years have gone by since the earliest delinquency date.

Once a judgment is entered, the property stays on hold for two years. Redeeming in that window costs the judgment amount, interest, a 5% penalty and a fee, and either the owner or a lienholder may pay it. Should the property be worth more than the debt, the owner is due the surplus after the county takes it.

Selling is one way to stop that clock. A cash sale can pay the old years out of proceeds at closing, and the Taxation office at 541-774-6541 can give you the balance for each year.

Jackson County charges $99.00 for a one-page deed (bargain and sale, quitclaim, warranty or transfer on death), with $5.00 for each added page. A trust deed or mortgage is $116.00. Call the Clerk at 541-774-6152 to confirm the current amount.

A document missing required first-page information carries a $20.00 non-standard fee. Regular copies are $4.00 for the first page, and certified copies are $7.75.

Start with the tax account, then the land. A few checks save the most trouble:

  • Ask Taxation for the balance of each open year.
  • Confirm whether the parcel has a farm or forest special assessment, since ending that use can trigger extra tax.
  • Ask whether any special assessment, fee or charge is attached to the account.
  • For fire-damaged or rebuilt property, ask the Assessor how the value was set.

Land that loses farm status can owe extra tax going back up to 10 years, or five inside an urban growth boundary. Rogue Valley orchard and vineyard parcels are exactly the type of land this affects.

Once you take an offer, the title company orders a tax report and asks Taxation for a payoff on each open year. They will want the deed, any deferral paperwork, and for an inherited house, proof of who has authority to sign.

At the closing table your proceeds cover the old years, interest and any special charge, and the Clerk's office records the new deed. Leave a few days for a deferral lien, because the state release is separate from the county payoff and can take weeks to post.

Seniors and disabled owners sometimes use the state deferral program. The Department of Revenue pays the county on the owner's behalf and records a lien, which must be repaid, with 6% simple interest, before it is released. A deferral account therefore has a payoff figure at closing, and release takes about eight weeks after payment posts.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Jackson County, Oregon?
faqs.a: Medford. Jacksonville was the first seat in 1853, and the seat moved to Medford in 1927 after the railroad bypassed Jacksonville.

faqs.q: How much is the early payment discount on Jackson County property tax?
faqs.a: It is 3% for paying in full by November 15, and 2% for paying two-thirds by that date. The one-third plan has no discount.

faqs.q: What is the Jackson County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, filed with the Property Value Appeals Board after you receive your statement. If that date is a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jackson County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At Room 111A, 10 S Oakdale Ave, Medford, Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM. Drop boxes are open 24 hours a day, and the phone number is 541-774-6541.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jackson County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid years are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Call the Taxation office for the balance of each year, because payments are applied to the oldest year first and interest is 1.333% a month.
